title: Prayer request acceptance can race into a database integrity error
reasoning: The accept endpoint checks for an existing acceptance, then creates a new row in a separate operation. The model enforces uniqueness on (prayer_request, user), so two near-simultaneous accept requests from the same user can both pass the exists() check; one create succeeds and the other raises IntegrityError, producing a 500 instead of the endpoint's intended 'already accepted' 400 response.
reproduction: Send two concurrent POST requests as the same user to /api/prayer-requests/{id}/accept/ for an approved request. Both can pass the exists check before either insert commits; the second insert violates the unique_together constraint.
recommendation: Use get_or_create inside a transaction and handle the created=False case with the existing 400 response, or catch IntegrityError and return the same idempotent error response.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not cover PrayerRequestAcceptance concurrency or duplicate accept submissions through the API.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused test that patches or simulates the create path raising IntegrityError after the existence check and asserts the API returns the duplicate-acceptance response instead of propagating a server error.
minimumFixScope: PrayerRequestViewSet.accept acceptance creation block and a duplicate/concurrency regression test.
